mainTopic: Whether רבי מאיר follows a person's first words (״תמורת עולה תמורת שלמים״), and the exact wording of the משנה on mixed intentions (כזית כזית / כזית וכזית) with לוי's question to רבי
overview: The amud opens with אביי challenging רב דימי. רבה בר בר חנה reported that, according to רבי יוחנן, רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי do not argue about the principle of following a person's first words. אביי explains that both agree on the clear cases: 'this, and afterward that' means only the first holiness takes effect, and 'this only if that' means both take effect. They argue only about someone who said ״תמורת עולה תמורת שלמים״. רבי מאיר reads the repeated ״תמורת״ as a change of mind, while רבי יוסי reads it as making the whole animal each offering. רב דימי answers that he simply disagrees with רבה בר בר חנה. The גמרא then asks whether the משנה about two wrong intentions reads 'כזית, כזית' or 'כזית וכזית', and why that small 'and' matters for רבי יהודה. It brings לוי's question to רבי about one כזית meant for 'tomorrow, outside', which רבי called a wise question and ruled is עירוב מחשבות. The amud explains why the question was wise for לוי, who learned only the version without 'and', and why he chose to ask that case. The amud ends just as the גמרא starts to describe how רבי would react in anger, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: אביי cites רבי יוחנן saying רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי do not argue
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב דימי with a teaching of רבה בר בר חנה in the name of רבי יוחנן: on the basic principle, רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי do not disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But didn't רבה בר בר חנה say in the name of רבי יוחנן that when you look closely at רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי, they do not disagree with each other?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב דימי's claim that רבי מאיר follows a person's first words. He quotes another report of רבי יוחנן's view that says the two תנאים do not argue at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי made the argument about a general rule: do we only follow a person's first words? אביי has a source in which רבי יוחנן says רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי agree on that rule. So רב דימי's version of רבי יוחנן seems to contradict this one.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)
When you get to the bottom of them / examine them closely

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רב דימי, who had just said that רבי מאיר follows a person's first words.

phrases.english: But doesn't Rabba bar bar Chana
say that Rabbi Yochanan said:
When you get to the bottom of them,
Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei
do not disagree with one another!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי, וְהָא רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב דימי's earlier report, which comes from before this passage
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's claim that רבי מאיר follows a person's first words
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A different report of רבי יוחנן's view says רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי agree on the principle, so it cannot be the source of their argument.

steps.title: But they clearly do argue
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי objects: how can you say they do not disagree, when the משנה plainly shows them arguing?
steps.simpleTranslation: And they don't disagree?! But they clearly do disagree!
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי pushes back on אביי. In the משנה, רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי give different rulings, so how can anyone say they don't argue?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה about ״תמורת עולה תמורת שלמים״ records two different rulings. So the claim that they 'do not disagree' seems to clash with an explicit argument. This sets up אביי's explanation in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: They certainly disagree (the doubled verb adds emphasis)

phrases.english: And they don't disagree?!
But they clearly do disagree!
phrases.notes: He means the משנה where they give different rulings for ״תמורת עולה תמורת שלמים״.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counter-challenge to אביי's claim in step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי do not disagree
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה explicitly records them giving different rulings.

steps.title: They argue only on the specific case, not on the principle
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that they argue only about their specific case, but not about the general principle.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: They disagree where they disagree, and they do not disagree where they do not disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that yes, they argue, but only about one particular case. They agree on the broader principle of how to treat two statements.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי separates the case from the principle. The argument in the משנה is real, but its source is not a general rule about 'first words.' It comes from how to read one particular phrasing, which the גמרא will spell out next.

keyTerms.meaning: In the matter where they disagree
In the matter where they do not disagree

phrases.english: He said to him: They disagree where they disagree,
phrases.notes: Here אביי is answering: they argue about the specific case in the משנה.

phrases.english: and they do not disagree where they do not disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: פְּלִיגִי בְּמַאי דִּפְלִיגִי, וְלָא פְּלִיגִי בְּמַאי דְּלָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב דימי's objection in step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the argument (case versus principle)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since they argue in the משנה, they must argue about the general principle of following first words.
steps.terutzMaskana: They argue only about one specific phrasing and agree on the general principle.

steps.title: Where everyone agrees: two clear kinds of statements
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר יוסף quotes רבי יוחנן: everyone agrees that 'let this take effect and afterward that' means the second does not take effect, and that 'this only if that' means both take effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי יצחק בר יוסף said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Everyone agrees that if he said 'Let this take effect and afterward let this take effect,' all agree the second does not take effect. If he said 'This shall not take effect unless that takes effect,' all agree it does take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing the areas where רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי agree. This backs up אביי's claim that they share the same principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone clearly sets an order ('this first, then that'), the first holiness takes hold and the second cannot. If he clearly makes the first depend on the second, both take hold. Since both תנאים agree on these clear cases, their argument cannot be about a general rule of 'first words.'

phrases.english: As Rabbi Yitzchak bar Yosef said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
All agree that where one says
phrases.notes: "All" means רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: 'Let this take effect, and afterward let that take effect' —
phrases.notes: The first "this" is the holiness of an עולה, the second is a שלמים. Some versions leave out the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: everyone agrees it does not take effect;

phrases.aramaic: ״לֹא תָּחוּל זוֹ אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן חָלָה זוֹ״ –
phrases.english: 'This shall not take effect unless that takes effect' —
everyone agrees it does take effect;

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's answer by showing what both sides agree on
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי share the same basic principle
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יצחק בר יוסף in the name of רבי יוחנן

steps.title: Where they do argue: the repeated word 'substitute'
steps.stepSummary: They argue when someone says ״תמורת עולה תמורת שלמים״. רבי מאיר reasons that repeating ״תמורת״ shows the person changed his mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where they disagree is when he says: 'A substitute for an עולה, a substitute for a שלמים.' רבי מאיר holds: since he could have said 'a substitute for an עולה and שלמים,' but instead said 'a substitute for an עולה, a substitute for a שלמים,' learn from this that he was retracting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now pins down the exact case of the argument and gives רבי מאיר's reasoning. It is about how to read one specific way of speaking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the person meant both holinesses together, the natural wording would be one ״תמורת״ followed by 'עולה and שלמים'. Repeating ״תמורת״ suggests he first meant an עולה and then tried to switch to שלמים. So for רבי מאיר, his ruling depends on reading these specific words, not on a general rule of 'first words count.'

keyTerms.meaning: A substitute animal that takes on the holiness of the animal it replaces
He is retracting / changing his mind

steps.confusionAlert: On אביי's explanation, based on רבה בר בר חנה's report of רבי יוחנן, רבי מאיר is not following a general rule of 'only the first words count.' His reasoning is about the wording: the repeated ״תמורת״ shows the person changed his mind. In step 7, רב דימי does not accept this reading.
steps.whatToRemember: On אביי's explanation, based on רבה בר בר חנה's report of רבי יוחנן, רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי agree on the clear cases. Their argument is only about the phrase ״תמורת עולה תמורת שלמים״, which רבי מאיר reads as a change of mind. רב דימי disagrees (step 7).

phrases.english: Where they disagree is where he says:
'A substitute for a burnt offering, a substitute for a peace offering.'
Rabbi Meir holds:
Since he should have said
'A substitute for a burnt offering and a peace offering,'
and he said instead 'a substitute for a burnt offering, a substitute for a peace offering' —
learn from this
that he was retracting.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי פְּלִיגִי, דְּאָמַר: ״תְּמוּרַת עוֹלָה תְּמוּרַת שְׁלָמִים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After showing where they agree, the גמרא now shows where they argue and why
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, the repeated ״תמורת״ shows the speaker retracted his first intention.

steps.title: Why רבי יוסי says the double phrase
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי explains that repeating 'תמורת' is not a change of mind. It shows the speaker wants the whole animal to be a substitute for each offering, not half for one and half for the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוסי says: if the person had said 'a substitute for an עולה and a שלמים', I might think he meant half the animal for an עולה and half for a שלמים. That is why he said 'a substitute for an עולה, a substitute for a שלמים': to show that all of it should be an עולה and all of it a שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives רבי יוסי's reason for the same words 'תמורת עולה תמורת שלמים', to balance רבי מאיר's reason from step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר read the repeated word 'תמורת' as a sign the person changed his mind. רבי יוסי reads it the opposite way: the person repeated it on purpose so that no one would split the animal in half. On this reading their argument is about what these particular words mean, not about the general rule.

keyTerms.meaning: That is to say; to show
All of it; the whole thing

steps.whyThisMatters: This supports אביי's claim from step 3: on this reading, רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי argue only about how to read this one phrase, and neither one is taking a side on the general principle. רב דימי disagrees in step 7.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yosei holds:
if he had said: 'A substitute for a burnt offering and a peace offering,'
I would have said
half is a substitute for a burnt offering
and half is a substitute for a peace offering;
that is why he said:
phrases.notes: 'He' is the person making the swap, not רבי יוסי himself.

phrases.english: 'A substitute for a burnt offering, a substitute for a peace offering'
to say that all of it is a burnt offering
and all of it is a peace offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes step 5 by giving רבי יוסי's side of the same case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי, the repeated 'תמורת' shows the speaker wants the whole animal to be a substitute for each offering, not a half-and-half split.

steps.title: רב דימי keeps his view that they disagree
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי tells אביי: רבה בר בר חנה says they do not disagree, but I say they do.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי said to אביי: he (רבה בר בר חנה) says they do not disagree, but I say they do disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי does not accept אביי's challenge. He openly admits his opinion differs from the teaching that was quoted to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי does not try to reconcile the two teachings. He simply says this is an argument between scholars about how to explain רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי. In his view, רבי מאיר really does hold that we follow only the first thing a person says.
steps.whatToRemember: The challenge from רבה בר בר חנה's teaching does not defeat רב דימי. He holds that רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי argue about the principle itself, while רבה בר בר חנה holds they do not.

phrases.english: He said to him:
he says they do not disagree,
phrases.notes: 'He' means רבה בר בר חנה, whose teaching אביי quoted in step 1.

phrases.english: but I say they disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הוּא אָמַר לָא פְּלִיגִי, וַאֲנָא אָמֵינָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the exchange between אביי and רב דימי by rejecting the force of אביי's challenge.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge only shows that another scholar disagrees with רב דימי. That cannot force רב דימי to change his own view.

steps.title: Which wording does the משנה use?
steps.stepSummary: עולא (or רב אושעיא) asks whether the Babylonian scholars know if the משנה reads 'כזית, כזית' or 'כזית, וכזית'.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said, and some say it was רב אושעיא: perhaps our Babylonian colleagues know: do we learn 'an olive-bulk, an olive-bulk', or do we learn 'an olive-bulk and an olive-bulk'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about a person who had two wrong intentions at once, one about time and one about place. It asks exactly how the person's words are worded in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only difference between the two versions is the small word 'and' (ו). That one letter might show whether the two intentions are joined together or are two separate statements. This matters for the argument between רבי יהודה and the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-bulk, the minimum amount that counts

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions describe the same two intentions: an olive-bulk beyond its time and an olive-bulk outside its place. The question is only whether the word 'and' joins them.

phrases.english: Ulla said,
and some say it was Rav Oshaya:
perhaps our colleagues, the Babylonians, know
do we learn 'an olive-bulk, an olive-bulk',
phrases.notes: He means an olive-bulk beyond its time and an olive-bulk outside its place, the case in our משנה.

phrases.english: or do we learn 'an olive-bulk and an olive-bulk'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of תמורה and returns to the wording of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה's wording includes the word 'and' between the two olive-bulk intentions.

steps.title: What each wording would mean
steps.stepSummary: Two options. Maybe the משנה says 'כזית כזית', and with 'and' everyone agrees it is a mixing of intentions. Or maybe it says 'כזית וכזית', so רבי יהודה treats even that as separate, and all the more so without 'and'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe we learn 'an olive-bulk, an olive-bulk'. Then if he said 'an olive-bulk and an olive-bulk', everyone agrees it counts as a mixing of intentions. Or perhaps we learn 'an olive-bulk and an olive-bulk', which means that for רבי יהודה it still counts as a separate statement. Then all the more so if he said 'an olive-bulk, an olive-bulk'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the two sides of the question so we can see what is at stake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: רבי יהודה follows the first intention only when there is no 'and'. With 'and', even he agrees the intentions are joined, which is called עירוב מחשבות. Option two: the משנה already has 'and', so רבי יהודה treats the first intention as separate even then, and certainly when 'and' is missing.

keyTerms.meaning: A mixing of intentions; the two wrong intentions count together instead of the first one deciding

steps.whatToRemember: The open question is whether the word 'and' makes רבי יהודה agree that the two intentions are mixed together. The משנה's exact wording decides how far רבי יהודה's view goes.

phrases.english: Either we learn 'an olive-bulk, an olive-bulk',
but with 'an olive-bulk and an olive-bulk'
everyone agrees it is a mixing of intentions;
or perhaps we learn 'an olive-bulk and an olive-bulk',
so that according to Rabbi Yehuda it is a separate statement,
and all the more so 'an olive-bulk, an olive-bulk'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out what depends on the question asked in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהודה's view, that the first intention decides, applies even when the word 'and' joins the two intentions.

steps.title: לוי asks רבי about one olive-bulk with both intentions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a story: לוי asked רבי about intending to eat one כזית tomorrow and outside. רבי calls it a real question and rules that it is עירוב מחשבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: לוי asked רבי, 'If someone intended to eat one olive-bulk tomorrow and outside, what is the law?' רבי said, 'This is a real question! It is a mixing of intentions.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story as a possible proof for the question about the wording of the משנה. This story sets up the discussion in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a single כזית carries both bad intentions at once, 'tomorrow' (פיגול) and 'outside' (only פסול). רבי rules that even רבי יהודה would call this עירוב מחשבות, so it does not become פיגול. The next steps will show what this teaches about the versions of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: He intended (had a thought during the עבודה)
Tomorrow (after the allowed time, which brings פיגול)
Outside (its proper area, which makes it only פסול)
A mixing of intentions, so it is not פיגול

phrases.english: Come and hear,
that Levi asked of Rabbi:
If he intended to eat an olive-bulk
tomorrow, outside, what is the law?
He said to him: This is a real question!
It is a mixing of intentions.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דִּבְעָא מִינֵּיהּ לֵוִי מֵרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to try to settle the question in Step 9 about the wording of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: Which version of the משנה רבי taught, and which cases count as עירוב מחשבות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of לוי's question to רבי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One כזית meant for both tomorrow and outside is עירוב מחשבות, so it is not פיגול.

steps.title: רבי שמעון ברבי says the answer is already in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי's son objects: why call it a great question? The משנה lists the cases where רבי יהודה disagrees, which implies that any other case is עירוב מחשבות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון the son of רבי said before him: Isn't this our משנה? 'To eat an olive-bulk outside, an olive-bulk tomorrow; an olive-bulk tomorrow, an olive-bulk outside; half an olive-bulk outside, half an olive-bulk tomorrow; half an olive-bulk tomorrow, half an olive-bulk outside: it is פסול and there is no כרת.' So any other case is a mixing of intentions!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון ברבי challenges his father's praise of לוי's question. He says the משנה already gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists specific cases where the חכמים say 'פסול, no כרת', and רבי יהודה argues only on those. Since לוי's case is not on the list, it must be one where everyone agrees it is עירוב מחשבות. So the question seems too easy to deserve praise.

keyTerms.meaning: Spiritual cutting off, the punishment for eating פיגול
The other case (the one not listed)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon, son of Rabbi, said before him:
Isn't this our Mishnah?!
To eat an olive-bulk outside, an olive-bulk tomorrow;
an olive-bulk tomorrow, an olive-bulk outside;

phrases.aramaic: כַּחֲצִי זַיִת בַּחוּץ כַּחֲצִי זַיִת לְמָחָר;
phrases.english: half an olive-bulk outside, half an olive-bulk tomorrow;

phrases.aramaic: כַּחֲצִי זַיִת לְמָחָר כַּחֲצִי זַיִת בַּחוּץ –
phrases.english: half an olive-bulk tomorrow, half an olive-bulk outside –
it is disqualified, and there is no karet for it.
So the other case is a mixing of intentions!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי's statement in Step 10 that לוי asked a real question.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lists only certain cases as disputed, so the unlisted case is clearly עירוב מחשבות. There was nothing to ask.

steps.title: רבי answers: for you, who learned two versions, it is easy
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers his son: לוי asked a wise question. For you it is not hard, because I taught you two versions of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He asked me a matter of wisdom, and you say 'our משנה'?! For you, whom I taught two versions, it is not difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי defends his praise of the question. He starts by explaining why it looked easy to his son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי had taught his son both versions, 'כזית כזית' and 'כזית וכזית'. With both versions listed, the son could see that the unlisted case, לוי's single כזית, is עירוב מחשבות. The next step explains why לוי could not see this.

keyTerms.meaning: A wise matter, a smart question

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הוּא שָׁאַל בִּי דְּבַר חָכְמָה,
phrases.english: He said to him: He asked me a matter of wisdom,
and you say 'our Mishnah'?!
For you, whom I taught two –
phrases.notes: The two versions are 'כזית כזית' and 'כזית וכזית', the question from Step 8.

phrases.english: it is not difficult for you;

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא שָׁאַל בִּי דְּבַר חָכְמָה, וְאַתְּ אָמַרְתָּ מִשְׁנָתֵינוּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing between learners: it depends on which versions of the משנה each one learned.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה clearly answers לוי's question, so it was not a wise question.
steps.terutzMaskana: The answer is clear only to someone who learned both versions.

steps.title: Why לוי had a real doubt
steps.stepSummary: לוי learned only one version and heard others learning two. He did not know which version was exact, so he could not tell whether his case was left out on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: But for him, whom I taught only one version, and who heard the Rabbis learning two, he thought: Maybe my version is exact, and their extra case is a mixing of intentions? Or maybe their version is exact, and my version simply left a case out. And since my version left out this case, maybe theirs also left out that other case?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי finishes his answer by explaining לוי's confusion. Because of it, the question really was wise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If לוי's single version is exact, the extra version others learned might be agreed-upon עירוב. Then nothing can be learned from what the list leaves out. But if the others' version is exact, then the משנה sometimes leaves cases out, and maybe it also left out לוי's case even though it is disputed. So the silence of the משנה could not settle the question for לוי.

keyTerms.meaning: They recite, they learn the text

steps.whatToRemember: A list in a משנה only teaches by what it leaves out if we are sure the list is complete. לוי was not sure, so his question was a wise one.
steps.confusionAlert: 'דידי' (mine) and 'דידהו' (theirs) are spoken from לוי's point of view: 'mine' is the one version he learned, and 'theirs' is the two versions the other חכמים learned.

phrases.english: For him, whom I taught only one,
and he heard the Rabbis reciting two –
and he thought: Maybe mine is exact,
and theirs is a mixing of intentions?
Or perhaps theirs is exact,
and in mine, it simply left a case out;
and since it left this out of mine –
perhaps it also left that one out of theirs?
phrases.notes: 'That one' is לוי's own case, one כזית meant for both tomorrow and outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי's answer by explaining why לוי's question was not obvious.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the doubt of a learner who knew only one version of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anyone could infer from the משנה's list that לוי's case is עירוב מחשבות.
steps.terutzMaskana: לוי could not tell whether the list was complete, so the question was a real one.
steps.whyThisMatters: The story shows that רבי taught both versions, 'כזית כזית' and 'כזית וכזית'. That bears on the question raised in Steps 8 and 9.

steps.title: Which version did רבי teach לוי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which wording לוי learned. It rules out the 'כזית וכזית' version, because with that wording nothing would be left out for לוי to wonder about.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which version did רבי teach לוי? If you say he taught him 'a כזית and a כזית', then nothing is really left out of the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants to know which of the two versions of the משנה לוי learned. It tests the first option and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 said לוי could not tell whether his case was left out on purpose. If he had learned the 'and' version, where רבי יהודה treats even 'a כזית and a כזית' as separate, the other wordings would already be covered. So there would be no real gap to make him wonder.

keyTerms.meaning: Which version did he teach him?
If you say (an option the גמרא is about to reject)
Something left out of a list

phrases.english: And which version did he teach him?
If you say he taught him 'a כזית and a כזית'
then this is not something left out!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which of the two versions mentioned in step 13 לוי actually learned.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which wording of the משנה לוי received from רבי.

steps.title: לוי learned 'כזית כזית' without 'and'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רבי taught לוי the version 'a כזית, a כזית', with no 'and'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he taught him 'a כזית, a כזית'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the question: לוי learned the version without 'and'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this version, the case with 'and' is still an open question. So לוי really had reason to wonder whether cases missing from the list were left out on purpose.

phrases.english: Rather, he taught him 'a כזית, a כזית'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by choosing the remaining option.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: לוי learned the 'כזית כזית' version, without 'and'.

steps.title: Then לוי should have asked about the 'and' case
steps.stepSummary: If לוי learned the version without 'and', his obvious doubt was the 'and' case. So why did he ask about 'a כזית tomorrow outside' instead?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him ask about 'a כזית and a כזית'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges לוי's choice of question. The doubt his version left open was the 'and' wording, not the case he actually asked about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The version לוי learned leaves 'a כזית and a כזית' unclear. That seems like the natural thing to ask, so his question to רבי looks off-target.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him ask (a challenge: he should have asked this)

phrases.english: Then let him ask about 'a כזית and a כזית'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges לוי's question in step 10, using the conclusion of step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: לוי's choice to ask about 'כזית למחר בחוץ'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His version left the 'and' wording unclear, so that is what he should have asked about.

steps.title: Ask one question, learn two answers
steps.stepSummary: לוי thought: if I ask about the 'and' case and the answer is 'separate', I still won't know about 'tomorrow outside'. So he asked about 'tomorrow outside' to learn more from one question.
steps.simpleTranslation: He thought: I will ask him one thing so that I learn two. If I ask about 'a כזית and a כזית', it works out well if he tells me it counts as one combined statement, since then all the more so 'a כזית tomorrow outside'. But if he tells me it counts as separate statements, I will still have a question about 'a כזית tomorrow outside'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why לוי chose his question: he wanted one answer that would settle two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'A כזית tomorrow outside' is one piece of food with two intentions, so it is more joined together than 'a כזית and a כזית'. If even the 'and' case counts as one combined statement, the more joined case surely does. But if the 'and' case counts as separate, the more joined case would still be unclear, so asking about the 'and' case might teach him only one thing.
steps.confusionAlert: 'כללא' here does not mean a general rule. It means the words count as one combined statement, so the intentions mix. 'פרטא' means each intention counts by itself.

phrases.english: He thought: I will ask him one thing
so that I learn two.
For if I ask about 'a כזית and a כזית'

phrases.aramaic: הָא נִיחָא אִי אָמַר לִי כְּלָלָא,
phrases.english: it works out well if he tells me it is one combined statement,
since then all the more so 'a כזית tomorrow outside';
but if he tells me they are separate statements

phrases.aramaic: אַכַּתִּי ״כְּזַיִת לְמָחָר בַּחוּץ״ קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לִי.
phrases.english: I will still have a question about 'a כזית tomorrow outside'.

steps.triggerLanguage: סְבַר: אִיבְעֵי מִינֵּיהּ חֲדָא דְּשָׁמַעְנָא תַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends לוי's choice of question against step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Strategic explanation: the chosen question was meant to cover more ground.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לוי should have asked about the 'and' case, since that was his clear doubt.
steps.terutzMaskana: Asking about the 'and' case could leave 'tomorrow outside' unanswered, so לוי asked about 'tomorrow outside' instead.

steps.title: His actual question has the same problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers back: asking about 'tomorrow outside' also teaches two things only if the answer is 'separate'. Since the answer was 'combined', the 'and' case is still open.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, now too: it works out well if he tells him 'a כזית tomorrow outside' is separate statements, since then all the more so 'a כזית and a כזית'. But if he tells him it is one combined statement, he still has a question about 'a כזית and a כזית'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that step 17's reasoning cuts both ways, so it does not explain לוי's choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even the more joined case, 'tomorrow outside', counts as separate, then the 'and' case surely does too. But רבי actually ruled that it is עירוב מחשבות, meaning one combined statement, so the 'and' case was still left unanswered. Both questions might teach only one thing, so step 17 does not explain why לוי preferred his question.

phrases.english: If so, now too:

phrases.aramaic: הָתִינַח אִי אָמַר לֵיהּ ״כְּזַיִת לְמָחָר בַּחוּץ״ פְּרָטָא,
phrases.english: it works out well if he tells him 'a כזית tomorrow outside' is separate statements,
since then all the more so 'a כזית and a כזית';
but if he tells him it is one combined statement,
he still has a question about 'a כזית and a כזית'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks step 17 by turning its own reasoning around.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation in step 17 that לוי's question would teach two things.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each question teaches two things only under one possible answer. 'Tomorrow outside' teaches two only if the answer is 'separate', and the answer was 'combined'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This leaves לוי's choice of question unexplained again, so the גמרא needs a new answer. Step 19 gives it.

steps.title: If the answer were 'combined', רבי would get angry
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 18. If רבי answered 'combined' about 'tomorrow outside', and the 'and' case also had that answer, רבי would get angry at לוי for asking the wrong question. So לוי would still learn something.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he would get very angry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 18 by saying רבי would react with anger. This line sets up the next line, which gives the words רבי would say in his anger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 claimed that a 'combined' answer about 'tomorrow outside' leaves the 'and' case open. The גמרא answers that רבי's reaction is also a source of information. If the 'and' case were also 'combined', רבי would be annoyed that לוי skipped the more obvious question. So if רבי does not get angry, לוי learns the 'and' case is different.

keyTerms.meaning: If so. Here it means: if רבי answered 'combined' and the 'and' case were also 'combined'.
He would surely get angry. The doubled verb makes it strong.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new rule about פיגול. It only explains how לוי could learn from רבי's reaction, not just from his words.

phrases.english: If so
he would surely get angry:
phrases.notes: רבי would be angry at לוי. What he would say comes in the next line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 18 and defends לוי's reasoning from Step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to another way לוי gets information: רבי's angry reaction, not only his answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A 'combined' answer about 'tomorrow outside' would leave the 'and' case unresolved (Step 18).
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with a 'combined' answer, לוי would learn about the 'and' case. If it were also 'combined', רבי would get angry that לוי asked the wrong question.
